title: Why Nasa spacecraft collided with asteroid – and the huge crater it caused

  • The European Space Agency has released the first images of the asteroid Dimorphos following NASA's deliberate spacecraft crash into it in 2022.
  • The images reveal that the collision left a stadium-sized crater across Dimorphos, altering its overall shape and causing it to tumble chaotically.
  • The impact successfully altered the asteroid's trajectory around the larger asteroid Didymos, shortening its orbital period by approximately 33 minutes.
  • Unveiled at the Natural History Museum in Berlin, the findings demonstrate a major step forward in developing reliable planetary defence against potential asteroid threats.
  • The Hera spacecraft will continue to investigate the asteroid system, taking higher-resolution images before deploying two miniature satellites in January 2027.
